title: Browser History
statement:
Design the history of a single browser tab. The tab starts on a home page, and from there you can visit new pages and move back and forward through the pages you've seen. Write a `BrowserHistory` class, built from the home page, with three operations:

- `visit url` goes from the current page to `url`. It clears the forward history, so after a visit there's nothing to go forward to.
- `back steps` moves back up to `steps` pages and returns the page you end up on. When fewer than `steps` pages are behind you, you stop at the home page.
- `forward steps` moves forward up to `steps` pages and returns the page you end up on. When fewer than `steps` pages are ahead of you, you stop at the last one.

The first line is the home page. The second line is the count `q`. Each of the next `q` lines is one operation. Print the answer to each `back` and `forward` on its own line. Pages have no spaces, the same page can show up more than once in the history, and `steps` is at least 1.

Input:

```text
home.com
10
visit a.com
visit b.com
visit c.com
back 1
back 1
forward 1
visit d.com
forward 2
back 2
back 7
```

Expected output:

```text
b.com
a.com
b.com
d.com
a.com
home.com
```

hints: Picture two piles of pages: the pages behind you, with the current page on top, and the pages ahead of you, with the next one on top.

Going back moves the top page from the first pile to the second, one step at a time, and going forward moves it back again. Stop early when there's nothing left to move, and never move the home page off the first pile.
A visit puts the new page on the first pile and empties the second one.
